SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT NO.XII, AT VIJAYAPURA, IN M.V.C.NO.476/2016, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY MOHAMMAD NAWAZ J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING::
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the claimant/injured seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal vide judgment dated 01.06.2018 passed in MVC.No.476/2016.
02.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company and perused the material on record.
The appellant/claimant sought for a total compensation of `.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident which took place on 07.11.2015 at about 07.15 p.m.
At the time of accident, he was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-31-S-4562.

According to him he was proceeding to his house on the said motorcycle and near the land of one Ningappa Govaroji on Vijayapura-Jamakhandi road, a Bolero Jeep bearing its Reg.No.KA-48-5023 was wrongly parked on Sadashiv vs Babu And Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64499217/
2 the middle of the road without putting any signal and his motorcycle hit against the said vehicle, due to which he sustained fractural injuries and his motorcycle also got damaged
. Immediately, he was taken to KLE, Hospital, at Jamakhandi and then shifted to Sanjeevini Hospital, at Vijayapura and he spent more than `.3,00,000/- for the medical treatment.

04. The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, was pleased to award a total compensation of `.3,02,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant under the following heads:-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7427-DB Sl.
Compensation Particulars No. awarded 01.
Injury, pain, and sufferings `.0,30,000=00 02.
Medical expenses `.1,81,216=00 03.
Food and Nourishment `.0,10,000=00 04.
Conveyance charges `.0,10,000=00 05.
Attendant charges `.0,10,000=00 06.
Loss of Amenities `.0,60,000=00 `.3,01,216=00 Total (rounded off to `.3,02,000=00).

05. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that, the appellant had sustained permanent disability to an extent of 25% to the whole body, however, the Tribunal has not taken into consideration the said permanent disability and therefore, he submits that the same has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
He contends that the compensation awarded even under other heads, in view of the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant, is also on a lower side.

Therefore,
he seeks to enhance the compensation.

The learned counsel for the appellant further contends that, the findings recorded by the Tribunal that the appellant was also negligent in riding the motorcycle and causing accident is erroneous and therefore, fixing 10% liability on him is liable to be set aside.
He contends that the Bolero Jeep was parked on the middle of the road without putting any signal and therefore, no negligence could have been attributed to the appellant.

07. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 has vehemently contended that the Tribunal has rightly come to the conclusion, after perusing the disability certificate/Ex.P.19 that the claimant is not having any loss of future income due to the said disability mentioned therein.

She contends that the claimant without taking proper care was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the Bolero Jeep on its rear side and therefore, he was also responsible for Sadashiv vs Babu And Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64499217/
3 the accident.
She would point out that the charge-sheet is also filed against the claimant.

Therefore,
she seeks to dismiss the appeal.
According to the appellant, on the date of accident he was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 31-S-4562 and a Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48-5023 was wrongly parked on the middle of the road.

It is contended that as it was dark, appellant could not see the said vehicle, since parking light was not on and therefore, accident occurred solely due the negligence of the driver of the said vehicle.
09. It is no doubt true that there is no material to show that, the parking light of the Bolero vehicle which was parked, was switched on.
However, if the appellant was cautious enough and slow in riding his motorcycle, there was possibility that he could have avoided the accident to some extent.
It is not in dispute that in the charge-sheet, appellant has been arraigned as accused No.2.
It is contended by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that appellant did not possess the driving license and there was no insurance policy to the motorcycle.
In that view of the matter, it cannot be said that there is no contributory negligence on the part of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:7427-DB appellant.

The Tribunal has rightly fixed the contributory negligence on the part of appellant at 10%, which does not call for any interference.
10.

Insofar as the injuries sustained by appellant is concerned, as per Ex.P.5/wound certificate, it is seen that he has sustained cut lacerated wound over the face extending from forehead, root of the nose, lateral wall of the nose, upper lip and lower lip and upto lateral side of the mandible region.
He has suffered comminuted fracture of mandible maxillary bone, nasal bone and frontal bones.
The wound certificate further discloses that C.T. Scan was taken, as per which comminuted depressed fracture of frontal bone, facial bones etc., were noticed.
The injuries are grievous in nature.
As per Ex.P.16 it is seen that he was operated for his ORIF for fracture of maxillary bone and mandible and depressed fracture of frontal bones.

11. The appellant has examined the Doctor/PW.3, who issued the disability certificate/Ex.P.19,
wherein he has stated that the appellant is having craniectomy defect on forehead.
He has stated that the appellant had visited NC: 2023:KHC-K:7427-DB his hospital on 07.11.2015. with history of road traffic accident and on that day he was treated by surgery for the head injury.
Though, the disability certificate was issued on 19.02.2018, the doctor has stated that the appellant was admitted in the hospital on 07.11.2015 with history of road traffic accident.

PW.3/Neurosurgeon has examined the appellant on 06.02.2018 for the purpose of disability and after follow up MRI Brain plain study, he has stated that anterio frontal on left side old injury with postsurgical status, anterior bilateral medial and basifrontal lobe, shows old insult with porecephalic cystic changes and volume loss.
PW.3/Doctor has opined that total permanent physical impairment for post head injury convulsions is 25%, compared to the whole body.
12. The Tribunal was not proper in holding that the appellant is not having loss of future income.

We are of the considered view that the appellant will suffer to certain extent due to the accidental Sadashiv vs Babu And Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64499217/
4 injuries which will have an impact on his earning capacity.
We quantify the permanent disability at 10% to the whole body.
The appellant was aged about 25 years at the time of accident and according to him, he was having an income of `.15,000/- per month.
However, there is no material placed to substantiate his income.
Considering the year of accident, it is just and proper to compute the income of the appellant at `.8,000/- per month.
The appropriate multiplier for the age group of the appellant is 18.
Hence, the appellant is entitled for `.1,72,800/- (`.8,000/- x 12 x 18 x 10 / 100) towards loss of future income.
14. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant, sum awarded towards injuries, pain and sufferings is enhanced from `.30,000/- to `.60,000/-.
Sum awarded towards food and nourishment is enhanced from `.10,000/- to `.20,000/-.
Sum awarded towards conveyance charges is enhanced from `.10,000/- to `.20,000/-.
Sum awarded towards attendant charges is enhanced from `.10,000/- to `.20,000/-.
A sum of `.16,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7427-DB laid up period.
Sum awarded towards medical expenses and loss of amenities is unaltered.
Hence, the appellant is entitled for a total compensation of `.5,50,000/- as against `.3,02,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Food and  `.0,10,000=00 `.0,20,000=00 nourishment Conveyance charges `.0,10,000=00 `.0,20,000=00 Attendance charges `.0,10,000=00 `.0,20,000=00 Loss of amenities `.0,60,000=00 `.0,60,000=00 Loss of income during  - `.0,16,000=00 the laid-up period Loss of future income - `.1,72,800=00  `.3,01,216=00 `.5,50,016=00 Sadashiv vs Babu And Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64499217/
5 Total (rounded off to (rounded off to  `.3,02,000=00) `.5,50,000=00)

In view of the above, we proceed to pass the following:
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7427-DB ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed in part.
II. The judgment and award dated 01.06.2018 passed by the Court of III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XII, Vijayapura in MVC.No.476/2016 is hereby modified.

III.
Appellant/claimant is entitled for a total compensation of `.5,50,000/- as against `.3,02,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
IV. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
V. The liability of respondents No.1 and 2 is joint and several at 90% of total compensation.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount before the Tribunal within a period of 06 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
The Compensation amount shall be released in favor of the appellant / claimant, on due identification.
